title: Finite-index transfer and natural prism for individual internal coefficient modules
statement: Let A be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. Let G be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group and H an open subgroup, with its compact subspace topology. Fix an internal-function presentation F and bar diagrams B for G and B_H for H [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Write U_H for restriction of the condensed action along H → G [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. There are natural cochain maps r : C_G → U_H C_H and t : U_H C_H → C_G and, for every equivariant internal A-module N [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], a homotopy h_N from t_N r_N to [G:H] times the identity of C_G(N). Each homotopy component is natural in every equivariant A-linear map N → P. Restriction r is pinned by the following evaluation: for every p ≥ 0, profinite test set S, section x of the internal functions from G^p to N over S, map f : T → S and continuous tuple g : T → H^p, evaluation of r(x) at (T,f,g) equals evaluation of x at (T,f,inclusion ∘ g), using the recorded bar-term identifications. All maps are internal A-module morphisms. This assertion concerns individual coefficient modules only; it neither introduces a coefficient complex nor asserts descent through a second differential or any cohomology identity.

proof.text: For the two fixed groups G and H use the homogeneous coordinates of [lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates]: homogeneous cochains are precisely the equivariant sections of internal functions on tuples, and Phi/Psi are prefix products/successive quotients. At the Lean interface these presentations must be constructed for the fixed B and B_H, rather than assuming a family of bar diagrams for every group. Choose S using exists_finiteRightTransversal and rho using finiteCosetRetraction_properties in [lem-sfb-finite-coset-homogeneous-averaging]; these group-theoretic helpers require no coefficient field. Then x=rho(x)s(x), rho(hx)=h rho(x), rho restricted to H is the identity, and card(S)=[G:H]. For a_s(x)=s inverse rho(sx), right multiplication induces a coset permutation pi_a with a_s(ax)=a a_(pi_a(s))(x).

proof.text:
On generalized homogeneous functions prescribe
$$(TF)(x_0,\ldots,x_p)=\sum_{s\in S}s^{-1}F(\rho(sx_0),\ldots,\rho(sx_p)).$$
Each summand is internal linear: pull back along the continuous tuple map, then apply the constant section $s^{-1}$ of the coefficient action. The evaluation interpretation of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] makes this a sheaf map before imposing homogeneity. To check homogeneity put $sa=h_su$ with $u=\pi_a(s)$. Then $\rho(sax)=h_s\rho(ux)$ and $s^{-1}h_s=au^{-1}$, so $TF(ax)=aTF(x)$ by reindexing the finite sum. For a variable $a:T\to G$, partition $T$ by the finitely many values of the locally constant permutation $\pi_a$. These are clopen profinite subobjects covering $T$; the same computation holds on each and hence on $T$ by the sheaf axiom. Coordinatewise substitution commutes with every deletion; the constant coefficient actions commute with finite sums. Therefore $\delta T=T\delta$. For $G$-homogeneous $F$, $s^{-1}F(\rho(sx_i))=F(a_s(x_i))$, giving $TR=\sum_s a_s^*$.

proof.text:
On all internal function cochains set $K=\sum_{s\in S}P_{1,a_s}$ using [lem-sfb-internal-function-vertex-prism], where $1:G\to G$ is the identity map. It gives $\delta K+K\delta=\sum_s a_s^*-|S|1=TR-[G:H]1$ and $K_0=0$. This sum preserves the homogeneous submodules: its evaluation is
$$(KF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{p-1})=\sum_s\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_{p-1})).$$
After replacing every $x_j$ by $ax_j$, covariance $a_s(ax)=aa_{\pi_a(s)}(x)$ extracts the coefficient action $a$ from $F$ and permutes the $s$-sum. For generalized $a$ use the same finite clopen partition as in step 2. Thus $K:B_G^p\to B_G^{p-1}$ internally, and the displayed homotopy identity restricts to $B_G$.

proof.text: Conjugate the transfer and sum of prisms by the homogeneous coordinate isomorphisms. The restriction square identifies the resulting restriction with precomposition along H^p → G^p. This yields natural cochain maps r,t and a homotopy rt to [G:H] on each coefficient module N. Substitutions, finite sums and coefficient actions commute with every equivariant module map, so both chain maps and each homotopy component are natural in N. All components are internal maps. In degree zero the prism identity has only its outgoing-differential term. For H=G choose the singleton transversal and zero homotopy. No differential on N and no vertical or horizontal homology is involved.

theorem internal_bar_coefficient_transfer (A : Ring.{u}) (G : Type u)
    [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (H : OpenSubgroup G) [CompactSpace H.toSubgroup]
    (F : InternalFunctions A) (B : BarDiagram (G := G) F)
    (BH : BarDiagram (G := H.toSubgroup) F) :
    let v : H.toSubgroup →ₜ* G :=
      { H.toSubgroup.subtype with continuous_toFun := continuous_subtype_val }
    ∃ r : cochains B ⟶ Profinite.CondensedAction.inflate (R := A.toMon) v ⋙ cochains BH,
    ∃ t : Profinite.CondensedAction.inflate (R := A.toMon) v ⋙ cochains BH ⟶ cochains B,
    ∃ h : ∀ N : Equivariant A G,
      Homotopy (r.app N ≫ t.app N) (H.toSubgroup.index • 𝟙 ((cochains B).obj N)),
      (∀ (N : Equivariant A G) (p : ℕ) (S : Profinite.{u})
        (x : sections A ((F.functor (power G p)).obj N.module) S)
        (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (g : C(T, power H.toSubgroup p)),
        (F.evaluate (power H.toSubgroup p) S N.module
          (((B.term N p).inv ≫ (r.app N).f p ≫
            (BH.term
              ((Profinite.CondensedAction.inflate (R := A.toMon) v).obj N) p).hom).hom.hom.app
              (op S) x)).val T f g =
        (F.evaluate (power G p) S N.module x).val T f
          (ContinuousMap.comp
            ⟨fun x i ↦ (x i : G), continuous_pi fun i ↦
              continuous_subtype_val.comp (continuous_apply i)⟩ g)) ∧
      (∀ (N P : Equivariant A G) (f : N ⟶ P) (i j : ℕ),
        ((cochains B).map f).f i ≫ (h P).hom i j =
          (h N).hom i j ≫ ((cochains B).map f).f j)
